VibePascal v56 -- aarch64-linux native compiler (runs on ARM64 Linux, e.g. a
64-bit Raspberry Pi).  An inferred inline var initialised from a real constant
is a Double, whatever the constant's value happens to be.
Source commit: a187bbac34 (merge of inlinevar-real-default)
Compiler fix:  f06e46d8eb  (compiler/pstatmnt.pas, compiler/defutil.pas, compiler/ncnv.pas)
Parent release: v55 (eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-built on x86_64-linux via a freshly bootstrapped
       compiler/ppcrossa64.v56 (itself built from a187bbac34)
Binary: bin/ppca64  md5 96241cbc8871786eb790c3c068258e33
                    sha256 d4c3fc42fd35fa8b7496fdd17c238f70bd9bf43b3e4cdc2b2116bc271e98fbfd

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  Only compiler/{pstatmnt,defutil,ncnv}.pas changed between
v55 and v56: no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change.  An
existing v54/v55 aarch64-linux unit set stays valid, and the utility binaries
are unchanged and not re-shipped.

WHAT CHANGED
  An inline var with no type annotation used to take its type from the real
  constant you initialised it with, and that type changes with the VALUE:

      var a := 1.0;      // Single   -  4 bytes,  7 digits
      var b := 0.1;      // Extended - 10 bytes, 19 digits
      var c := 1.0/3.0;  // Single, or Extended under {$mode delphi}
      var d := 1/2;      // Double

  v56 infers the DEFAULT real type -- Double -- in either direction.  RANGE is
  never traded: 1.0e400 and 1.0e-4000 keep their wider type, because a Double
  would silently hold +Inf and 0.  A variable or non-constant expression keeps
  its own type, and an explicit `single(1.0)` still wins.  How real CONSTANTS
  themselves are typed is NOT touched -- that is stock upstream FPC.

VERIFIED ON THIS PLATFORM BY EXECUTION, NOT BY INSPECTION
  Every number below came from running real aarch64 instructions under
  qemu-user-static on the build host: the COMPILER is an aarch64 binary run
  under the emulator, and each program it produced was RUN too, not merely
  linked.

  A/B against the PUBLISHED v55 aarch64 binary (md5 7a41c2c459ebe303ecf47907d9e13f74,
  taken out of its own shipped tarball and md5-checked against that tarball's
  VERSION.txt before it was trusted as a control):

    tinlinevarrealinfer1.pp, three modes, the mode being a real axis here
      -Munleashed              v55 exit 1, 27 failing checks  ->  v56 exit 0, 52/52
      -Mdelphi                 v55 exit 1, 18 failing checks  ->  v56 exit 0, 49/49
      -Mdelphiunicode          v55 exit 1, 18 failing checks  ->  v56 exit 0, 49/49
    The control FAILS in every mode, so a pass here cannot be reached by accident.

    tinlinevarrealinfer2.pp is a %FAIL test -- `for var i := 1.0` must stay
    rejected.  BOTH compilers reject it, cleanly, with "Ordinal expression
    expected" and zero internal errors.  The fix did not open that door.

  NO REGRESSION, also by execution, on the v56 compiler:
    tinlinevarnativeint1.pp   PASS   (NativeInt inference, v54's rule)
    tinlinevarstrinfer1.pp    PASS   (default-string inference, v54's rule)
    tblockscopefinal1.pp      PASS   (block-scoped finalisation: every corner
                                      released exactly once -- counted, not
                                      merely observed as "released")

  LIMIT, stated plainly: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real shipped
  bytes and real ARM64 encodings, so codegen and RTL defects DO surface -- but
  it is not a Raspberry Pi.  NOBODY HAS RUN THIS ON PHYSICAL ARM HARDWARE.
  Cache behaviour, real kernel and libc versions and timing are outside what
  this can show.  Do not quote a pass here as a hardware sign-off.
  Re-runnable: sh dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh
